# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

## Respondents → the public account each story is based on

Superintendents (PRIMARY link, Parts 1 and 2):

- Ray Villanueva → [OPU] a former site inspector: "try to remember everything you wanted to write. Sometimes you'd fill in gaps from memory" — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791 ; delays and weather in the log from [KOE]
- Hank Sorensen → author's invention, filling a gap: a chipped (rather_not_say) story, so the reader sees one GUESSED-by-code person.
- Luis Arreola → author's invention, filling a gap: a vague, habitual story with no one occasion (GUESSED), echoing [YCP] "for hours in their trailers".
- Jolene Pruitt → author's invention, filling a gap: a gate No (between jobs in the window).
- Curtis Baines → author's invention, filling a gap: a gate No (a job in closeout, no site walks that week).
- Kwame Asante → [HN] "these photos aren't very searchable" and the practitioner comment that reports get filled with filler: "fill up some reports with random bullshit just so the project moves forward" — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42208610 ; OneDrive and "hundreds of photos" — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42207501
- Gary Lindqvist → the thread's hallucination sceptics, transposed to a superintendent who signs his own log — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42207216 and https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42209501
- Priya Raman → [LYC] "Fresco saves supes hours they’d otherwise spend double-entering notes."; texting the crew from [HN]; the owner-side PM walk from the general-contractor comment on change orders and tracking — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42207501
- Dwayne Hollis → [LYC] the group is "superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.)": an assistant super writes the log (the Current-solution escape). Author's invention beyond that.

Contractor operations leads (COMMERCIAL_B2B link, Part 3 only; no story by rule). Their picks are the author's, shaped by:
- Renee Castillo → [HN] the price as offered and "unlimited users"; author's invention for the picks.
- Bill Ostrowski → the price-sceptic comment: "$1k is like way way way out of the reasonable range", "a fraction (e.g. 10%)" — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42215232
- Faith Nakamura → author's invention, filling a gap: supers do the logs on their own time, so the firm counts no cost.
- Gordon Achebe → [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" on a large job; author's invention for the picks.
- Sandra Whitfield → the same price-sceptic comment ("cheaper to get them to do it than buy software at $12k p.a.") — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42215232
- Omar Haddadin → author's invention, filling a gap: a buyer who cannot recall the cost or the budget source (both escapes).
- Lena Brandt → the AEC engineer's comment that integration with existing products drives buying — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44043729 ; author's invention for the picks.
- Trevor McAllister → author's invention, filling a gap: a firm paying a part-time document controller (an amount, not hours).

No respondent carries the name of a commenter, customer or founder.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

insights.line: What made the others more pressing?

whys.g1: Both answers are about the schedule slipping and subs not showing up, so one group named in plain site words is exactly how I'd sort them.
whys.g2: There's no junk or off-topic answer on this line, so nothing junk got into the group.

founder.order_why: The recall-window screen (4) sits between two identical context screens (3 and 5), so I define the context, pick the window, then seem to be back on the same context page before reaching the problem.
founder.asked_twice: Screens 3 and 5 ask the same question, 'Before we test anything, let's define exactly where this idea applies.'
founder.missing: Nothing about the solution: narrated site-walk videos turned into notes, texted to the crew and pushed to Procore or ACC in one click. Nothing on the price ($1k per site per month, less for multi-site or multi-month terms) or the cost it replaces. Nothing on the buyer: the general contractor pays per site, not the superintendent. As shown, the flow tests only the problem with superintendents and never reaches the contractor operations leads who decide to buy.

PRIMARY.order_why: Asking which thing I'd most like made easier before asking how the photo upload on my last log actually went puts my wish ahead of my recall of what happened, so the photo question should come before screen 4.
PRIMARY.missing: How long typing up the log and uploading photos took me after the walks, and where my photos and notes were (phone, notebook, texts) before they went into Procore.

screens.why1: Naming the project is the obvious first step before anything else is typed into the flow.
screens.why2: A plain one-line question any founder answers on first reading.
screens.why3: I know what my own company is called, so I can answer it straight from my own life.
screens.why4: A free-text box with no options, rows or chips.
screens.why5: The name I typed, 'Fresco — the scribe for construction superintendents', is shown as I wrote it.

screens.why1: Right after naming the project, asking which country I sell into first is the obvious next setup step, and it decides the units, the wage and the people the study goes to.
screens.why2: "Where will you sell this first?" is plain to any founder, and US is how I'd say it.
screens.why3: I know I'm selling to US general contractors first, since we're driving around the Bay Area to their sites.
screens.why4: A country picker with an optional region covers it; US with no region is my true answer, and leaving the region empty is a fair way to say "the whole country".
screens.why5: It stores exactly what I mean, US with no narrower region, and the kicker uses my own line about the scribe for superintendents.

screens.why1: Pinning down who, what job, when and which crowd is the obvious first step before Keel tests anything about my idea, and it comes right after I named the project and picked the US.
screens.why2: The four boxes are plain, but 'every belief you give later... is read inside this boundary' is abstract tool-talk that I'd read twice to see it just means 'we only ask supers in this situation'.
screens.why3: These are my own customers, their trailer at the end of the day and their Procore logs, all things I know from the site walks.
screens.why4: The screen shows four type-in boxes and a read-back, no options or chips to judge.
screens.why5: My typos are fixed and the meaning holds, but 'who have jobs that run on Procore or ACC' with its stray comma reads looser than my 'whose jobs run on Procore or ACC', as if the supers own the jobs rather than the jobs running on the platform.
screens.instead: Keep the four boxes; change the intro to 'Four short answers, a phrase each: who, what they're trying to get done, when it happens, and which group. We'll only ask people who fit this.' and read back 'Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.'

screens.why1: Right after defining who and when, setting how far back a superintendent's last daily log can be is the obvious next piece of the context, and the summary confirms the rest before it.
screens.why2: 'Episode' is researcher's language, not mine; I'd say 'the last time they did the daily log', though the intro and the 'last 5 working days' line make it clear on a second read.
screens.why3: I know supers do the log every working day on a five-day site week, so picking a window of 5 working days is squarely from what I know of my customers.
screens.why4: A count with a working-days unit fits a site week exactly, and the chip I picked says what I meant.
screens.why5: The summary keeps my actor, job, circumstance and segment as I typed them, and '5 working days' is my window unchanged.
screens.instead: How recent should their last daily log be to count? (chips: the last 5 working days / the last 2 weeks / the last month)

screens.why1: After I've set the window, reading back the whole context for one yes before testing anything is exactly where this belongs, even though it reuses screen 3's heading.
screens.why2: Site walks, daily log, Procore, ACC, general contractors and working days are all my everyday words; only 'who have jobs that run on' reads a touch clunkier than my 'whose jobs run on'.
screens.why3: It describes my own customers and the end-of-day trailer work I built Fresco around, so confirming it is something I know cold.
screens.why4: A confirm chip ('Yes, that's it') alongside a way to edit is all a readback card needs, and nothing is missing.
screens.why5: Every field I typed is there nearly word for word, but 'on commercial jobs' from my plural actor is dropped, and commercial GCs are who I'm selling to.
screens.instead: Superintendents on commercial jobs at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC. When the day's site walks are done and the photos and notes still have to go into the daily log, they want to keep an accurate record of the day's work on site. We'll ask about the last 5 working days. [Yes, that's it] [Edit]

screens.why1: Right after the context is pinned down, Keel restates the problem I typed so I can confirm it before the study tests it, which is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: Trailer, site walks, Procore, OneDrive, daily logs, punch lists and a dispute with the owner are all my trade's everyday words, though 'a great many photos' sounds stiffer than anyone on a jobsite talks.
screens.why3: It describes exactly what I watched supers do on those weekends in Napa, the South Bay and SF, so I can check it against what I know.
screens.why4: The screen shows a statement to read and confirm, with no options, chips or value box.
screens.why5: The spelling is cleaned up and the meaning holds, but my numbers are blurred: 'up to 3 hours a day' became 'hours every day' and '30-200 photos' became 'a great many photos', and those figures are the heart of my pitch.
screens.instead: Construction superintendents spend up to 3 hours a day on documents: they take 30-200 photos a day on their site walks, then spend hours at the end of the day in the trailer uploading them to Procore or OneDrive and typing daily logs and punch lists, mostly for liability or a dispute with the owner.

screens.why1: Right after I seeded the problem, Keel reads it back for me to confirm before it builds the study on it.
screens.why2: Site walks, trailer, Procore, daily logs, punch lists and a dispute with the owner are all words I and my supers use every day.
screens.why3: It is exactly the end-of-day grind I watched supers do in their trailers and built Fresco around.
screens.why4: A confirm-or-edit choice is all a read-back card needs, and "Yes, that's the problem" is the true answer.
screens.why5: It keeps my problem, but my 30-200 photos became "a great many", my "up to 3 hours a day" became a vague "hours", and ACC dropped out though my segment names Procore or ACC.
screens.instead: Construction superintendents spend up to 3 hours at the end of every day in the trailer, uploading the 30 to 200 photos from their site walks to Procore, ACC or OneDrive and writing daily logs and punch lists, mostly for liability or a dispute with the owner. [Yes, that's the problem] [Edit it]

screens.why1: Right after the problem card, asking how widespread I think the end-of-day log grind is comes next, and it is the first of the four belief questions the intro promises.
screens.why2: Every word is a super's word, but 'spent hours typing up the log and uploading photos' joins two chores, and it doesn't say whether that means on at least one day or every day, which the belief line ('at least once') settles and the question doesn't.
screens.why3: How many supers on Procore or ACC jobs are stuck in the trailer doing logs after the walks is exactly what I've seen on site visits and heard in every customer call.
screens.why4: Five bands cover 0 to 10 with no overlap, and 8 or more in 10 holds my 'nearly all'; the 'I'm not sure' escape from the intro fits a founder's belief.
screens.why5: It still means what I typed: the walks are done and the photos and notes still have to go into the daily log, with the 'hours' from my own launch posts.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, how many out of 10 construction superintendents spent hours on at least one day getting the day's photos and notes into the daily log after the site walks? (Fewer than 2 in 10 / 2 or 3 / 4 or 5 / 6 or 7 / 8 or more in 10 / I'm not sure)

screens.why1: Right after I guessed how many supers it hits, asking how many days of the week it hits is the obvious next question for a job that happens 'per day'.
screens.why2: Typing up the log, uploading photos and site walks are how I and every super I talk to describe the end of the day; the sentence reads clean on the first pass.
screens.why3: I've ridden along on site walks and watched supers sit in the trailer for hours afterwards, so I can give an estimate from what I have seen.
screens.why4: A low-high box in working days out of 5 fits a five-day site week, and 'I'm not sure' is the right escape for a founder's belief.
screens.why5: The belief line, 4 to 5 working days out of 5, is exactly what I entered, and 'spend hours ... after the site walks' keeps my 'few hours uploading' and 'up to 3 hours a day'.

screens.why1: Right after how many supes and how often, it makes sense to ask what else competes for their attention, so the log can be ranked against real headaches.
screens.why2: The words are mine, but tying 'what else is hard' to the moment the walks are done made me pause, because schedule, subs, RFIs and safety are not end-of-day trailer problems; they run all week.
screens.why3: I live in supers' trailers; I can name their other headaches without guessing.
screens.why4: The only option is the escape chip, and 'Leave this out of the study' fits a founder who would rather not rank the problem.
screens.why5: Keel's belief keeps the log as one of their two worst problems, but it reframes the comparison as 'five things that are hard in a week on site', which is broader than the end-of-day moment the question asks about.
screens.instead: Besides the daily log, what else is hard for construction superintendents in a week on a commercial job? Name up to four, e.g. schedule, subs, RFIs and submittals, safety.

screens.why1: Right after I named the other difficulties, it's the obvious moment to check the list my log problem will be ranked against.
screens.why2: Daily logs, subs, RFIs and submittals are everyday words in a super's trailer, and every row is short enough to hear once and get.
screens.why3: Every row is something a superintendent on a commercial job fights with in a normal week, so they can rank them from their own days.
screens.why4: 'Keeping the job on schedule' overlaps with 'Getting subs to show up and finish', since subs not showing is the main reason a job slips, so a super could split one worry across two rows.
screens.why5: The first row is my problem in my words, the photos and the log after the walks, and the five rows show nothing of Fresco or of the contractor paying.
screens.instead: Rows: Uploading photos and typing daily logs / Getting subs to show up and finish / Chasing RFIs and submittals / Keeping the site safe / Keeping the owner and PM updated

screens.why1: After establishing how often the log eats my evenings and how much it matters, asking how supers handle it today is the natural next question before the solution step.
screens.why2: 'Keep an accurate record of the day's work on site' and 'tools, habits, workarounds' are exactly how I'd talk about daily logs, photos and Procore uploads.
screens.why3: I've watched supers do this in their trailers and built the company on it, so I can answer straight from what I know.
screens.why4: It's a free-text box with one escape chip, and 'Leave this out of the study' is a sensible way out of a current-solution question.
screens.why5: The belief Keel drew, that uploading photos and typing the log in the trailer still falls short for most supers, is what I typed and what I believe, even though I left 'how well it goes' blank.

screens.why1: Right after asking how supers keep the record today, it makes sense to ask how well that way works, and for a daily log the plain measure is when it got done.
screens.why2: Four rows read like a super talks, but 'Done before leaving the site walks' is awkward: you finish a walk, you don't leave it.
screens.why3: Any super knows exactly when he closed out yesterday's log: on the walk, in the trailer, at home that night, or not at all.
screens.why4: The rows are ordered and distinct, but the first is oddly worded, and no row covers the super whose assistant or foreman wrote the log that day.
screens.why5: The belief matches my claim of hours in the trailer, but the stored bar points at 'Done in the trailer in under an hour', which is not one of the rows, while the box on screen says 'Done within an hour after the walks'.
screens.instead: When did yesterday's daily log get done? — Done as I walked the site / Done within an hour after the last walk / Took a couple of hours in the trailer / Ran into the evening or at home / Didn't get finished that day (chip: someone else wrote it)

screens.why1: Picking who will put the questions to my supers is the natural last step before the study goes out, and nothing earlier asked it.
screens.why2: The question is plain, but the hint packs in video, typing or tapping, a preselected voice, recording once and 400 credits, so I'd read it twice to see what I'm actually choosing and paying for.
screens.why3: I know my supers: guys in a trailer at end of day on their phones, so I can judge which voice they'd sit through.
screens.why4: Two voices, each with a 5-second sample, the default marked, nothing missing that I'd want at this point.
screens.why5: It keeps 'construction superintendents' as I typed it and shows nothing of my product or the buyer to the people being asked.

screens.why1: Right after choosing who asks the questions, picking how my superintendents answer before the link goes out is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: Talking, typing or tapping, and a voice that works in a quiet room versus a loud one, are plain to me; I know some supes will open this in a noisy trailer or truck. The doubled "Daphne Daphne" and the run-on "Hear her Still recording" read as layout glitches, not wording I'd stumble on.
screens.why3: I know how my supes use their phones at the end of the day, mostly short taps and voice, so I can choose from what I know.
screens.why4: AI voice, read-and-tap and let-them-choose cover the real choices, don't overlap, and the readiness notes tell me what each costs in waiting.
screens.why5: It keeps my group as "construction superintendents" and shows nothing of Fresco's product or pricing to anyone.

screens.why1: After choosing how superintendents answer, deciding who gets the link is the natural last step before sending.
screens.why2: Plain words a founder would use; 'Contacts page' is Keel's own screen and the descriptions explain each path.
screens.why3: As the founder I know whether I'm sending to supers I've met on walks, finding them, or posting in a group.
screens.why4: The three paths are distinct and complete, but the group option's 'signs in with Google' is a detail that will put off superintendents on site, and there is no hint which suits a trade group or a GC's internal channel.
screens.why5: My pick, people I know by name, is kept as typed and nothing of the product leaks.
screens.instead: Who gets a link? People I know by name (one link each) / People I found with Keel (pick a Contacts list) / A group I'm already in, like a trade forum or a GC's crew chat (one open link; each person signs in before the interview)

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits beside '4 answered', but it names only Frequency when Importance and Current solution are also too few, and the '5 needed' that decides it is only on the cards, not beside the verdict.
screens.why_b2: There is no chart here; the tally '1 holding · 3 too few' and Prevalence's 'bar 6 of 7 · at the bar' read plainly, but I had to look twice to see why 7 answered and 6 said yes yet only 4 counted on the next three cards.
screens.why_b3: Importance and Current solution carry the exact lines I checked on the way in, and Prevalence and Frequency read as my belief about logs after site walks in the last 5 working days.
screens.why_b4: '5 needed to call it' implies I need one more superintendent through the later questions, but nothing tells me to send the study to more supers or why three of my seven dropped out after Prevalence.
screens.why_b5: The n's are shown and the low counts are called too few, but my own claim that supers 'lose hours every day to documents' sits under the title like a finding, on a page where only Prevalence holds, and only just at the bar.

screens.why_b1: "Holding up" sits directly beside "6 of 7 said yes · bar 6 of 7 · at the bar", so the verdict and the number that decides it are tied together on one line.

screens.why_b5: n=7 stays visible, the count line says "a small group: a lean, not a call", and the So line limits the claim to "these 7", so nothing overreaches.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits beside '5 needed to call it', but the line under it says '4 answered' while the count line says 6 answered and 4 counted, so I have to work out that it means four counted.

screens.why_b3: 'Frequency' and the line 'type up their log after site walks on 4 to 5 working days out of 5' are my daily-log belief in my own terms.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic; it doesn't tell me that one more counted superintendent would decide it, or that every counted answer so far is in my band.
screens.why_b5: It refuses to call it on 4 counted, says 'a small group: a lean, not a call', and names who was left out and why, with no claim beyond the people who answered.
screens.instead: Too few to call: all 4 supers counted typed their log on 4 or 5 of the last 5 working days (6 answered, Hank and Luis not counted); one more counted answer settles it, so get one more superintendent to answer.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits right beside '4 answered · 5 needed to call it', so I know there's no verdict yet and exactly why.
screens.why_b2: The bars count picks (8) but my bar is drawn in people ('3 of 4'), so I need a second look to see that the '2' beside my problem means 2 people against a bar of 3.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits with its deciding number, 4 counted against the 5 needed, so I know why there is no call even though 3 of the 4 fell short.

screens.why_b3: The belief line is word for word the one I checked, about uploading photos and typing the log in the trailer still falling short, though the question asks only about photos while the answers are about the log.

screens.why_b1: The status word 'Too few to call' sits right beside '4 answered · 5 needed to call it', so I know there is no verdict yet and exactly which number decides it.
screens.why_b3: 'Importance' and the belief about uploading photos and typing daily logs being one of the two they would most like made easier are word for word what I checked on the way in.

screens.why1: A first screen asking whether my jobs run on Procore or ACC is the obvious gate for a study about daily logs on those platforms.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are the names every super at a GC uses daily, so I'd answer this on first read without thinking.
screens.why3: I know exactly what platform my current job is on, so this is straight from my own work.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it cleanly for a gate, and a screener carries no escape per §5.
screens.why5: It keeps the founder's Procore-or-ACC segment and leaks nothing about any product or scribe.
screens.why6: Short, one question, and 'Yes; or No' is easy to hold, though 'I'll read 2 options' is a touch stiff where §17 says a screener should end 'Yes or no.'

screens.why1: Right after asking if my jobs run on Procore or ACC, asking whether I did a daily log this week is the obvious next gate, though the kicker still says 1 of 4 like the screen before.
screens.why2: I'd answer it straight off, but I don't 'type up' my log; I fill out the daily log in Procore, half the time on my phone, so 'type up your log' is a little off from how I'd say it.
screens.why3: I do a daily log every working day after walking the site, so this is squarely my week.
screens.why4: Yes and No cover it, but the chips don't fit: 'I can't recall one particular daily log' makes no sense on a yes-or-no about the last five days, and 'I'd rather not say' is a second escape on a gate that shouldn't have one.
screens.why5: It drifted: the photos and notes going into the daily log became 'typing up your log', and the photos dropped out, though nothing of a product leaks to me.
screens.why6: Short, one question, 'Yes or no' at the end; I'd hear it once and answer.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you put the day's photos and notes into the daily log after your site walks? Yes · No

screens.why1: Right after I said yes to typing up my log after walks, asking on how many of those five days is the obvious next question.
screens.why2: Plain words I use every day: log, site walks, working days.
screens.why3: I know which days last week I did my daily log, so I can count them.
screens.why4: The numbers 1 to 5 cover it and the escape fits, but bare digits are not labelled as days.
screens.why5: It is about my own logging and nothing of anyone's product or plan comes through.
screens.why6: Short and one question, with 'a number from 1 to 5' easy to hold and the escape said last.

screens.why1: After asking how many days I typed up my log, it makes sense to ask where that sits against the rest of my week before going further.
screens.why2: RFIs, submittals, subs and daily logs are words I use every day, so I can answer it on first hearing.
screens.why3: Every one of these is part of my week as a super, so I can pick from what I actually lived.
screens.why4: Keeping the job on schedule and getting subs to show up and finish overlap for me, because subs not showing is the main reason I fall behind schedule, and owner meetings and inspections are missing.
screens.why5: The log option is in my own terms with no product or company name, and it sits fairly among the other headaches instead of being pushed.
screens.why6: One short question with five short parallel options and one escape at the end is easy to hold and answer by ear.
screens.instead: Think of your last week on site. Which one of these would you most like made easier? Chasing RFIs and submittals; keeping subs and the schedule on track; dealing with the owner and inspections; uploading photos and typing daily logs; or keeping the site safe. Or say none of these.

screens.why1: Asking how my last log went fits after I said which part I'd most like made easier, but it jumps straight to photo uploads as if that was my pick, even if I'd picked something else.
screens.why2: The question asks how uploading the photos went, but every option is about when and where the log got finished, so I'd have to read it twice to work out what I'm actually answering.
screens.why3: I upload photos to Procore and finish a daily log every day, so I know exactly how my last one went.
screens.why4: None of the options answer how the photo upload went (quick, slow, a couple of hours sorting and tagging, stuck on bad signal), so my true answer is missing, and 'Log done on site' doesn't match the question at all.
screens.why5: Nothing about a product leaks to me, but the question has drifted between two things, the photo upload and the whole log write-up, so it doesn't clearly mean either one.
screens.why6: It's short and the five options are easy to hold when heard, but after hearing a question about photos, the first option 'log done on site' sounds like an answer to something else.
screens.instead: Think of your last daily log. How long did getting the site photos into Procore take? — Under 15 minutes · 15 minutes to under an hour · An hour to under two hours · Two hours or more · I didn't upload photos that day — or say I can't recall.
